newsitem.title: UK: Economist Intelligence Unit welcomes India reform.
newsitem.headline: Economist Intelligence Unit welcomes India reform.

text.p: Reforms aimed at attracting $10 billion a year in foreign investment in India have been implemented more effectively and rapidly than expected, the Economist Intelligence Unit said in a report.

The London-based think-tank said that despite the anti-foreign rhetoric of India's election earlier this year, the United Front-Left Front government's industry ministry has not acted to cut foreign investment in "low priority" areas such as consumer goods.

"The Industry Ministry says that fiscal measures to discourage investment are a matter for the Finance Ministry which, with pro-reformer Palanaippan Chidambaram in charge, is unlikely to make such a move," the EIU said.

The governing coalition, which includes communists and leftists who had been viewed as hostile to foreign investment, is likely to improve on the reforms introduced by the previous Congress government, the EIU believes.
It notes that the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) met 10 times between July 12 and August 21 to clear 332 projects worth $2.6 bilion.
However, the EIU said the government's reforms still had room to make progress, specifically in expanding the proposed 74 percent limit on foreign equity investment in infrastructure.

"There is no great advantage to be had in giving foreign investors 74 percent equity over 51 percent. True, 74 percent will increase the investors' final dividend and give him some psychological reassurance that he is in control. But as recent events in India have shown, joint ventures do not always run smoothly, particularly those formed for no other reason than to meet regulatory requirements," the EIU said.

Citing a $328,571 proposed investment by Daimler Benz in a software project, the EIU said that because the German company had sought 100 percent ownership, it had to go through the bureaucracy of the FIPB, which was a waste of time and effort with so many major projects awaiting approval. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
